content: Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Additionally, erythromycin stearate can elevate rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised when these drugs are co-administered. Rilpivirine may enhance the toxicity of escitalopram by prolonging the QTc interval, and escitalopram can similarly increase rilpivirine toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Famotidine can reduce rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. This interaction may lead to treatment failure or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. Famotidine should be administered at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Fingolimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring during co-administration. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of flecainide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. Fluconazole can elevate rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but no rilpivirine dose adjustment is necessary. However, rilpivirine can increase fluconazole toxicity via QTc prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine may increase the toxicity of fluoxetine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Fosamprenavir can increase rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, rilpivirine is not expected to alter the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of foscarnet by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. Fostemsavir and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Gepirone and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Gilteritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. Granisetron and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of haloperidol by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Hydroxyzine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ibuprofen/famotidine can increase gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ibutinide and rilpivirine can mutually increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of iloperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of indapamide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Indinavir can elevate rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required. Isoniazid can increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of isradipine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Itraconazole can elevate rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but no rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole can increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but no rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. Clinical monitoring for breakthrough fungal infections is recommended when azole antifungals are co-administered with rilpivirine. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of lapatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Levoketoconazole can elevate rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but no rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. Clinical monitoring for breakthrough fungal infections is recommended when azole antifungals are co-administered with rilpivirine. Lithium and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir can increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine can also increase lopinavir toxicity via QTc prolongation. Caution and monitoring are required. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Magnesium chloride can reduce rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Magnesium gluconate can reduce rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of maprotiline by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. Mavorixafor can increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Rilpivirine can increase the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Methadone and rilpivirine can be co-administered without dose adjustments. However, rilpivirine can increase methadone toxicity via QTc prolongation.
